title: Client token runway & thresholds workbook — QBR prep (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is a client-facing QBR prep doc focused on short-term token runway, recent rate-limit events, and an operational playbook for automated alerts. Goal: give account team clear numbers to discuss at the QBR and a repeatable set of thresholds/actions to avoid unexpected throttles or billing surprises.

Quick executive summary (to fill before QBR):
- Last 30 days token consumption: [___ tokens] total, change vs prior 30d: [+/- __%].
- Peak per-minute token rate (observed): [___ tpm]. Rate-limit events: [__] in last 90d, longest incident: [__ minutes].
- Estimated runway at current pace (with buffer): [__ days / weeks]. Recommended immediate adjustment: [increase soft alerts | request quota bump | optimize batching].

Topline metrics (required inputs from billing dump):
- Monthly committed tokens (contract): [__]
- Billable tokens used to date this invoice period: [__]
- Unbilled overage to date: [__ dollars]  (calc = max(0, used - committed) * rate)
- Current token burn rate (tokens/day): [__]
- Historical 7d rolling median latency & per-token cost: [__ ms | $__ / 1k tokens]

Token spend timeline (fill rows in sheet):
- Date range | Tokens | Token delta (%) | Notable spike driver | Jira/PR reference | Owner
- 2025-01-15 — 2025-02-14 | [___] | [+X%] | release v2.3 internal test flood | GH PR #___ | Eng contact: Sam
- Notes to self: look for automated test suites hitting production endpoints, retention of KV cache across restarts, and any new published cron jobs.

Root-cause checklist for spikes (use during post-mortem):
- New client feature rollout? If yes, which route/model variant?
- Any bot / scraping pattern detected? (IP clusters, identical payloads)
- Long-form generation tasks increasing average tokens per request?
- Sudden change in sample length or use of streaming vs non-streaming?
- Cache miss rate increased after deploy?
- Billing config changed (metering window, commit applied late)?

Rate-limit incident log (example entries):
- 2025-01-29 14:12 UTC — returned 429 for route /v1/gen/chat — peak tpm 8k, duration 22 minutes, root cause: autoscaler lag on dedicated pool, fallback to hosted throttles. Action: raised soft-alert threshold, requested temporary capacity burst.
- 2024-12-05 09:40 UTC — repeated token warnings then overage charge applied; customer on payg with daily cap set too low. Action: alerted account owner and adjusted budget alert.

Budget runway calculator (fill-in):
- Inputs: remaining prepaid token balance = R, current avg tokens/day = B, safety buffer multiplier = S (default 1.25).
- Runway (days) = floor(R / (B * S)).
- Example: R=1,200,000 tokens, B=40,000 tokens/day, S=1.25 => runway = floor(1,200,000 / 50,000) = 24 days.
- Decision thresholds: <14 days => immediate outreach + temporary commit offer; 14–30 days => recommend smaller commit or throttle policy change; >30 days => normal cadence.

Suggested alert tiers & automated actions (implement via monitoring/alerts):
- Tier 1 (info): 60% of expected monthly burn, email account + CS owner (no auto actions).
- Tier 2 (soft warning): 80% runway or 85% committed consumption — SMS + Slack pings to on-call AE, generate in-console banner recommending commit/adjustment.
- Tier 3 (critical): 95% committed consumption OR sustained >90% of peak tpm for 15+ minutes — temporarily rate-limit non-essential routes, open PagerDuty incident for SE + CS, propose immediate short-term top-up.
- Billing safeguard: default daily spend cap option + auto-cutoff toggle (needs customer consent).

Playbook: immediate steps when Tier 3 triggers (fill owner names):
1) CS triage (owner: [AE name]) — confirm whether traffic pattern is legitimate. Use sample payloads and recent request IDs.
2) Engineering ops (owner: [SRE]) — check autoscaler logs, fallback routes, and model variant swaps; if autoscaler is saturated, enable emergency burst in Dedicated or route proportion to cheaper model.
3) Finance (owner: [Billing]) — notify about potential overages; prepare invoice note if immediate top-up accepted.
4) Customer comms (owner: [AE]) — send templated incident message with ETA for mitigation and recommended interim controls.

Renewal / upsell signals derived from usage patterns:
- Consistent 20%+ month-over-month growth in tokens for 3 consecutive months => recommend reserved capacity conversation.
- Frequent short-lived spikes tied to periodic batch jobs => propose scheduled batch window & committed burst plan.
- High peak-to-average ratio (>6x) with many 429s => propose model variant tiering and circuit-breaker implementation.

QBR slides & talking points (short script):
- Slide: Current consumption snapshot (committed vs used) — emphasize runway and immediate ask if under 14 days.
- Slide: Notable incidents and mitigations — 1–2 bullets per incident, resolution status.
- Slide: Cost-efficiency recommendation — batching, quantization, or model switch; show estimated $/month savings.
- Slide: Renewal recommendation — commit size, proposed term, and expected SLA/throughput improvements.

Data requests for engineering before QBR (deliverables):
- Per-route tpm time-series (1m granularity) for last 90d (CSV)
- Sample payloads for top 5 heavy requests during spikes
- Autoscaler scaling events and GPU utilization logs for incident windows
- Billing export with token-level granularity for invoice period

Action items (pre-QBR):
- [AE] Confirm top 3 contract clauses we can propose for quick commit (by 2025-02-18).
- [SRE] Provide peak-minute series and identified suspected causes (by 2025-02-17).
- [Finance] Precalculate overage scenarios for +10% / +25% / +50% burn (by 2025-02-18).

Notes, heuristics, and ‘gray-area’ decisions:
- If spikes are caused by internal QA or a newly shipped integration, treat as mitigatable and offer a one-time grace credit if customer agrees to follow-up remediation.
- If traffic appears to be abusive/bot-driven, prioritize rate-limits and consider security enforcement (WAF, IP block) rather than billing credits.
- When in doubt, escalate to solutions engineering for a short-term model-routing plan; easier to justify cost of temporary capacity than risk customer outage.

Templates (copy-paste into support/CS messages):
- Incident initial message (short): "We observed sustained elevated token usage impacting your quota (approx. [tokens/min]). We are triaging with engineering and will follow up within 30 minutes with mitigation steps. If you want us to apply a temporary limit or top-up, reply with "top-up"."
- Renewal/commit offer blurb: "Based on recent usage trends we recommend a [size] reserved plan to reduce unit costs by ~[__%] and avoid throttles during peak windows. Shall I send a 30-day limited commit agreement?"

Open questions / to resolve in QBR prep meeting:
- Does the customer prefer automated soft-throttles or manual CS approval to cut non-critical routes?
- Any internal enforcement (e.g., app-level backpressure) planned by customer within 30 days?
- Can we add a budget-alert webhook to their PagerDuty?

Appendix: quick formulas and conversion constants
- Tokens/day from samples = sum(tokens per request over sample window)/days
- Estimated dollars for overage = (tokens_over_commit / 1000) * overage_rate_per_1k
- Suggested safety multipliers: experimental workloads=1.5, steady-prod=1.15

(End of workbook — use as working doc for internal prep. Replace bracketed placeholders with actual values pulled from billing export before sharing with customer.)
